editorial:
Imagine moving to a new town and realizing your high school is actually a real-life fairy tale. You follow Ellie, a girl who starts at Avalon High and meets all the usual types: the star athlete, the popular cheerleader, and the moody rebel. At first, it feels like any other teen drama you have seen a million times. But as you watch, you start to notice that these kids are not just stereotypes. They are actually living out the legend of King Arthur and his knights. It is a cool mix of modern high school stress and ancient magic that keeps you guessing about who is actually who.

The acting is solid and the twists are fun, even if the plot feels a bit predictable if you know the Arthurian stories. It moves at a good pace and doesn't get bogged down in too much detail. If you love stories about hidden destinies and secret identities, you will really enjoy this one.
endingExplained: You find out that the students are reincarnations of the Round Table. Ellie discovers she is actually the true heir to the throne, not Will. In the final showdown, the true king is revealed, and the cycle of the legend is finally broken. Ellie accepts her role and helps her friends move past their ancient roles so they can finally just be normal teenagers and live their own lives.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves teen dramas with a magical twist.
